rows.name: Now
rows.detail: Today's fixes are in: no own wars before the strike, CP cut out of the strike's decisions, readiness by the take-the-city check, reachable targets only. Tonight two catches from your trio game: the strike now lasts until the target's capital falls (with releases when the capital can't be reached), and a crash in logged games is fixed (an empty army kept alive). Build ab-0f35217 is compiling; PC 2 plays one trial game on it, then 20 games vs greedy civs.

rows.name: EarlyStrike + StrikeList
rows.detail: Your opening, from the experts: follow the list, Honor/policy per civ, barbarian hunting, upgrade and go; strike stages from game state, no turn windows.

rows.detail: Late-spike civs (Zulu, Mongolia, China's Chu-Ko-Nu...) build up, then strike; warmongers without a reachable spike play the Composite Bowman rush.

rows.detail: At most 2 workers per 3 cities; work boats only for a city's own sea tiles (your call: a normal test).

rows.name: WondersForVictory
rows.detail: A world wonder only if it suits the civ's target victory, or is an economy wonder.
rows.test: Normal test after the attack work.

rows.name: GreedyWideDeals
rows.detail: A wide greedy civ out of room trades luxuries, open borders and research agreements more.

rows.name: GreedyWide / GreedyTall
rows.detail: Your two kinds of greedy: wide (Liberty, expand, then grow and trade) and tall (Tradition, 3-4 cities, tech and policy rush).

rows.detail: PC 2, 20 games vs greedy civs after trial28. Stops on any wonder or gift before the strike's declaration. Judged by captures, and how many by T80.

rows.detail: Expert rows for the most common aggressors are in; more civs as the data shows which plans work.

rows.detail: Each style beats one and loses to one. Waits until attacks take cities.

rows.name: Waiting flags
rows.detail: LeanBuilders, WondersForVictory, GreedyWideDeals: normal tests after the attack work.

rows.name: Trio: one of our three styles wins
rows.target: In a 6-player game with our greedy, balanced and aggressive civs and 3 CP civs, one of ours wins ≥ 90% of full games (the user's aim: every game)
rows.detail: Built. A first look (4 games to T150) had one of ours on top in 3 (75%), but our aggressor never attacked there. The real 20-game run waits until attacks take cities.

rows.name: Strength against CP
rows.target: ≥ 60% strength share against CP's AI (a milestone; strength is now the guard and quick test for each change)
rows.detail: 50.4% (C8, the 12 flags that passed, 6 pairs on PC 2). Economy and diplomacy fixes moved it only about half a point by T150; the big lever left is war, cities changing hands.

rows.name: Attack: an aggressor takes cities
rows.target: Against greedy civs (few units, no walls) several cities by T150; against balanced civs at most 1 per war
rows.detail: Getting closer: on the follow-the-list build Greece took a city at T59, like your Aztec at T54. Over the overnight expert blocks, 3 captures in 20 games. The next block is the first with every known leak closed.

rows.name: Matchup triangle
rows.target: Greedy beats balanced, aggressive beats greedy, balanced beats aggressive; no style wins overall
rows.detail: The three styles are coded (Personality). The matchup test waits until attacks reliably take cities.

rows.name: Deals with a purpose
rows.target: Deals help the civ win, or stop a civ it holds a grudge against from winning (your call: no deal quota)
rows.detail: The old count was fine anyway (1.7 new deals per civ per 10 turns). CP's victory rivalry only starts after T150, so this waits for full games.

rows.name: AI turn speed
rows.detail: C8 games average 5.6 s per AI turn. In split games both groups share one turn, so this needs an all-C run against an all-B run; not run yet.
